verses.text: Di word of di Lord wey come to Hosea, Beeri pikin, for di days of Uzziah, Jotham, Ahaz, and Hezekiah, kings of Judah, and for di days of Jeroboam, Joash pikin, king of Israel.

When di Lord begin to speak by Hosea, di Lord talk to Hosea, “Go, take for yourself wife of prostitution and children of prostitution, because di land don commit great prostitution, by departing from di Lord.”
So e go and take Gomer, Diblaim pikin, wey conceive and bear am son.
Di Lord talk to am, “Call im name Jezreel, because yet small while, and I go avenge di blood of Jezreel on di house of Jehu, and go cause di kingdom of di house of Israel to cease.
E go happen for dat day say I go break di bow of Israel for di valley of Jezreel.”
She conceive again, and bear daughter. Di Lord talk to am, “Call her name Lo Ruhamah, because I no go again have mercy on di house of Israel, to forgive dem at all.
But I go have mercy on di house of Judah, and go save dem by di Lord dem God, and go no save dem by bow, nor by sword, nor by battle, by horses, nor by horsemen.”
When she don wean Lo Ruhamah, she conceive, and bear son.
Di Lord talk, “Call im name Lo Ammi, because una no be my people, and I no be una God.

Yet di number of di children of Israel go be as di sand of di sea, wey no fit dey measured or numbered. E go happen say for di place where e dey talk to dem, ‘Una no be my people,’ e go dey talk to dem, ‘Una na children of di living God.’
Di children of Judah and di children of Israel go dey gathered together, and dem go appoint one head for demselves, and dem go go up out of di land, because great go be di day of Jezreel.”
“Say to your brothers, ‘Ammi!’ and to your sisters, ‘Ruhamah!’
Plead with your mother, plead, because she no be my wife, neither I be her husband, so make she put away her prostitution from her face, and her adulteries from between her breasts,
lest I strip her naked, and make her like di day wey she dey born, and make her like wilderness, and set her like dry land, and kill her with thirst.
Yes, I no go have mercy on her children, because dem na children of prostitution.

Because dem mother don play di prostitute. She wey conceive dem don act shamefully, because she talk, ‘I go go after my lovers, wey give me my bread and my water, my wool and my flax, my oil and my drinks.’
Therefore see, I go hedge up your way with thorns, and I go build wall against her, so that she no go find her paths.
She go chase her lovers, but she no go overtake dem. She go seek dem, but she no go find dem. Den she go talk, ‘I go go and return to my first husband, because den e dey better for me pass now.’
Because she no know say na I give her di grain, di new wine, and di oil, and multiply to her silver and gold, wey dem use for Baal.
Therefore I go take back my grain for di time of am, and my new wine for di season of am, and I go take away my wool and my flax wey suppose cover her nakedness.
Now I go uncover her lewdness for di sight of her lovers, and none go deliver her out of my hand.
I go also cause all her mirth to cease, her feasts, her new moons, and her Sabbaths, and all her solemn assemblies.
I go lay waste her vines and her fig trees, of which she don talk, ‘Dem na my wages, wey my lovers don give me.’ I go make dem forest, and di animals of di field go devour dem.
I go visit on her di days of di Baals, to whom she burn incense, and decorate herself with her earrings and her jewels, and go after her lovers, and forget me,” talk di Lord.
“Therefore see, I go allure her, and bring her into di wilderness, and speak comfortably to her.
From dere I go give her her vineyards, and di valley of Achor for door of hope. She go respond dere, as for di days of her youth, and as for di day wey she come up out of di land of Egypt.
For dat day,” talk di Lord, “you go call me ‘My husband,’ and no go call me ‘My Baal’ any more.
Because I go take away di names of di Baals out of her mouth, and dem no go dey mentioned by dem name any more.

For dat day I go make covenant for dem with di animals of di field, and with di birds of di sky, and with di creeping things of di ground. I go break di bow, and di sword, and di battle out of di land, and go make dem lie down safely.
I go betroth you to me forever. Yes, I go betroth you to me for righteousness, and for justice, and for loving kindness, and for compassion.
I go even betroth you to me for faithfulness, and you go know di Lord.
E go happen for dat day, I go respond,” talk di Lord. “I go respond to di heavens, and dem go respond to di earth.
Di earth go respond to di grain, and di new wine, and di oil, and dem go respond to Jezreel.
I go sow her to me for di earth. I go have mercy on her wey no get mercy. I go talk to dem wey no be my people, ‘You na my people,’ and dem go talk, ‘My God!’”
Di Lord talk to me, “Go again, love woman wey her lover love, even adulteress, even as di Lord love di children of Israel, though dem turn to other gods, and love cakes of raisins.”
So I buy her for myself for 15 pieces of silver, and one and half homers of barley.
I talk to her, “You go stay with me many days. You no go play di prostitute, and you no go belong to any man. Na so I go also be to you.”
Because di children of Israel go stay many days without king, and without prince, and without sacrifice, and without sacred stone, and without ephod or idols.
Afterward di children of Israel go return, and seek di Lord dem God, and David dem king, and go come trembling to di Lord and to im goodness for di latter days.
Hear di word of di Lord, una children of Israel, because di Lord get controversy with di inhabitants of di land, because no truth dey, nor goodness, nor knowledge of God for di land.
Swearing, lying, killing, stealing, and committing adultery dey. Dem break all bounds, and bloodshed touch bloodshed.
Therefore di land go mourn, and everyone wey dwell inside am go languish, with di animals of di field and di birds of di sky. Yes, di fish of di sea go dey taken away.
Yet make no man strive, nor reprove another, because your people dey like dem wey strive with di priest.
You go stumble for day, and di prophet also go stumble with you for night, and I go destroy your mother.

My people dey destroyed for lack of knowledge. Because you don reject knowledge, I go also reject you, so that you no go be priest to me. Seeing say you don forget di law of your God, I go also forget your children.
As dem dey multiplied, so dem sin against me. I go change dem glory into shame.
Dem feed on di sin of my people, and dem set dem heart on dem iniquity.
E go be, like people, like priest. I go punish dem for dem ways, and repay dem for dem deeds.
Dem go eat, and no get enough. Dem go play di prostitute, and no increase, because dem don stop to take heed to di Lord.
Prostitution, wine, and new wine take away di understanding.
My people ask counsel from dem wooden idol, and dem staff declare to dem, because di spirit of prostitution don cause dem to go astray, and dem don play di prostitute, departing from dem God.

Dem sacrifice on di tops of di mountains, and burn incense on di hills, under oaks and poplars and terebinths, because di shade dey good. Therefore una daughters play di prostitute, and una brides commit adultery.

I no go punish una daughters when dem play di prostitute, nor una brides when dem commit adultery, because di men demselves go aside with prostitutes, and dem sacrifice with temple prostitutes. Di people wey no understand go dey overthrown.
Though you, Israel, play di prostitute, yet make Judah no offend. No come to Gilgal, neither go up to Beth Aven, nor swear, “As di Lord live.”
Because Israel don dey stubborn, like stubborn heifer. Now di Lord go feed dem like lamb for wide pasture?
Ephraim don join to idols. Leave am alone.
Dem drink don turn sour. Dem play di prostitute continually. Dem rulers dearly love shame.
Di wind don wrap dem up for im wings, and dem go dey ashamed because of dem sacrifices.
“Hear dis, una priests, and listen, una house of Israel, and give ear, house of di king, because di judgment dey against una, because una don be snare for Mizpah, and net spread upon Tabor.
Di rebels don go deep into slaughter, but I go discipline all of dem.
I know Ephraim, and Israel no hidden from me, because now, Ephraim, you don play di prostitute. Israel dey defiled.
Dem deeds no go allow dem to turn to dem God, because di spirit of prostitution dey inside dem, and dem no know di Lord.
Di pride of Israel testify for im face. Therefore Israel and Ephraim go stumble for dem iniquity. Judah also go stumble with dem.
Dem go go with dem flocks and with dem herds to seek di Lord, but dem no go find am. E don withdraw imself from dem.
Dem don deal treacherously against di Lord, because dem don bear strange children. Now di new moon go devour dem with dem fields.
Blow di horn for Gibeah, and di trumpet for Ramah. Sound di alarm for Beth Aven. Tremble, Benjamin.
Ephraim go become desolation for di day of rebuke. Among di tribes of Israel I don make known wetin go surely be.
Di princes of Judah dey like dem wey remove di boundary. I go pour out my wrath on dem like water.
Ephraim dey oppressed, and crushed for judgment, because e dey determined to follow wetin no good.
Therefore I dey to Ephraim like moth, and to di house of Judah like rottenness.
When Ephraim see im sickness, and Judah see im wound, den Ephraim go to Assyria, and send to King Jareb. But e no fit heal una, neither cure una of your wound.
Because I go be to Ephraim like lion, and like young lion to di house of Judah. I, even I, go tear and go away. I go carry away, and none go deliver.
I go go and return to my place, until dem acknowledge dem offence and seek my face. For dem affliction dem go seek me earnestly.”
“Come, and make we return to di Lord, because e don tear us, and e go heal us. E don injure us, and e go bind us up.
After two days e go revive us. For di third day e go raise us up, and we go live before am.
Make we know, make we press on to know di Lord. Im going forth dey sure as di morning. E go come to us like di rain, like di spring rain wey water di earth.”
Ephraim, wetin I go do to you? Judah, wetin I go do to you? Because your love dey like di morning cloud, and like di dew wey go early.
Therefore I don cut dem by di prophets. I don kill dem by di words of my mouth. Di judgments on you dey like di light wey go out.
Because I desire mercy, and no sacrifice, and di knowledge of God more pass burnt offerings.
But dem, like Adam, don transgress di covenant. Dere dem don deal treacherously against me.
Gilead na city of dem wey work iniquity. E dey stained with blood.
As robbers wait for man, so di company of priests murder for di way to Shechem. Surely dem don commit lewdness.
For di house of Israel I don see horrible thing. Ephraim prostitution dey dere. Israel dey defiled.
Also, Judah, harvest dey appointed for you, when I return di captivity of my people.
When I wan heal Israel, den di iniquity of Ephraim dey uncovered, and di wickedness of Samaria, because dem commit falsehood. Di thief enter in, and di bandits dey raid outside.
Dem no consider for dem hearts say I remember all dem wickedness. Now dem own deeds don surround dem. Dem dey before my face.
Dem make di king glad with dem wickedness, and di princes with dem lies.
Dem all na adulterers, like oven wey di baker heat. E cease to stir di fire, from di time wey e knead di dough, until e dey leavened.
For di day of our king, di princes make am sick with heat from wine. E stretch out im hand with mockers.
Because dem approach with dem heart like oven, while dem dey lie in wait. Dem baker sleep all night. For morning e burn like flaming fire.
Dem all dey hot like oven, and devour dem judges. All dem kings fall. None among dem call to me.
Ephraim mix imself among di peoples. Ephraim na cake wey no dey turned.
Strangers don devour im strength, and e no know am. Yes, grey hairs dey here and dere upon am, and e no know am.
Di pride of Israel testify to im face, but dem no return to di Lord dem God, nor seek am, for all dis.
Ephraim dey like silly dove, without understanding. Dem call to Egypt. Dem go to Assyria.
When dem go, I go spread my net on dem. I go bring dem down like di birds of di sky. I go discipline dem, as dem don hear for dem congregation.
Woe to dem, because dem don wander from me! Destruction to dem, because dem don rebel against me! Though I redeem dem, yet dem don speak lies against me.
Dem no cry to me with dem heart, but dem howl upon dem beds. Dem assemble demselves for grain and new wine. Dem rebel against me.
Though I don train and strengthen dem arms, yet dem devise mischief against me.
Dem return, but no to di Most High. Dem dey like deceitful bow. Dem princes go fall by di sword for di rage of dem tongue. Dis go be dem derision for di land of Egypt.
“Put di trumpet to your lips! Di enemy dey come like eagle against di house of di Lord, because dem don transgress my covenant, and rebel against my law.
Dem go cry to me, ‘My God, we, Israel, know you.’
Israel don cast off di thing wey good. Di enemy go pursue am.
Dem don set up kings, but no by me. Dem don set up princes, but I no know am. Of dem silver and dem gold dem don make idols for demselves, so that dem go dey cut off.
Di calf of Samaria don dey cast off. My anger dey kindled against dem. How long dem go dey incapable of innocence?
Because e come from Israel, di craftsman make am, and e no be God. Yes, di calf of Samaria go dey broken in pieces.
Because dem sow di wind, and dem go reap di whirlwind. E no get standing grain. Di stalk go yield no head. If e yield, strangers go swallow am up.
Israel dey swallowed up. Now dem don dey among di nations like vessel wey nobody delight for.
Because dem don go up to Assyria, wild donkey wey dey alone. Ephraim don hire lovers.
Yes, though dem hire among di nations, now I go gather dem, and dem go begin to waste away under di burden of di king of princes.
Because Ephraim don multiply altars for sin, dem don become altars for am to sin.
Though I write for am di many things of my law, dem dey regarded as strange thing.
As for di sacrifices of my offerings, dem sacrifice flesh and eat am, but di Lord no accept dem. Now e go remember dem iniquity, and punish dem sins. Dem go return to Egypt.
Because Israel don forget im Maker, and build palaces. Judah don multiply fortified cities. But I go send fire on im cities, and e go devour di strongholds of dem.”
No rejoice for joy like di peoples, Israel, because you don play di prostitute, departing from your God. You don love di prostitute reward on every grain threshing floor.
Di threshing floor and di winepress no go feed dem, and di new wine go fail her.
Dem no go dwell for di Lord land. But Ephraim go return to Egypt, and dem go eat unclean food for Assyria.

Dem no go pour out wine offerings to di Lord, neither dem sacrifices go dey pleasing to am. Dem go be to dem like bread of mourners. All wey eat am go dey defiled, because dem bread go be for dem own hunger. E no go come into di house of di Lord.
Wetin una go do for di day of solemn assembly, and for di day of di feast of di Lord?
Because see, dem don go away from destruction, yet Egypt go gather dem up. Memphis go bury dem. Thorns go possess dem precious things of silver. Thorns go dey for dem tents.

Di days of visitation don come. Di days of recompense don come. Israel go know am. Di prophet na fool. Di man wey get di spirit dey mad, because of di abundance of your iniquity, and because di hatred dey great.
Ephraim na watchman with my God. As for di prophet, di snare of bird catcher dey in all im ways, and hatred for di house of im God.
Dem don deeply corrupt demselves, as for di days of Gibeah. E go remember dem iniquity. E go punish dem sins.

I find Israel like grapes for di wilderness. I see una fathers like di first ripe fruit on di fig tree for her first season. But dem come to Baal Peor, and consecrate demselves to di shameful thing, and become abominable like dat wey dem love.
As for Ephraim, dem glory go fly away like bird. No birth, no pregnancy, and no conception.
Though dem bring up dem children, yet I go bereave dem, so that no man go remain. Yes, woe to dem also when I depart from dem!
Ephraim, as I see am, dey like Tyre, planted for pleasant place. But Ephraim go bring out im children to di killer.
Give dem, Lord, wetin you go give? Give dem miscarrying womb and dry breasts.
All dem wickedness dey for Gilgal. Because dere I hate dem. Because of di wickedness of dem deeds, I go drive dem out of my house. I go love dem no more. All dem princes na rebels.
Ephraim dey stricken. Dem root dey dried up. Dem go bear no fruit. Yes, though dem bring forth, yet I go kill di beloved fruit of dem womb.
My God go cast dem away, because dem no listen to am. Dem go dey wanderers among di nations.
Israel na luxuriant vine, wey bear fruit for imself. According to di multitude of im fruit e don multiply altars. According to di goodness of im land dem don make di pillars good.
Dem heart dey divided. Now dem go dey found guilty. E go break down dem altars. E go destroy dem pillars.
Surely now dem go talk, “We no get king, because we no fear di Lord. Di king, wetin e go do for us?”
Dem speak words, swearing falsely in making covenants. Therefore judgment spring up like poisonous weeds for di furrows of di field.
Di inhabitants of Samaria go dey afraid for di calf of Beth Aven. Because im people go mourn over am, and im priests wey rejoice over am, for im glory, because e don depart from am.
E go also dey carried to Assyria for gift to King Jareb. Ephraim go receive shame, and Israel go dey ashamed of im own counsel.
As for Samaria, im king dey cut off, like twig on di surface of di waters.
Di high places of Aven, di sin of Israel, go dey destroyed. Thorns and thistles go come up on dem altars. Dem go talk to di mountains, “Cover us!” and to di hills, “Fall on us!”
Israel, you don sin from di days of Gibeah. Dere dem stand. Di battle against di children of wickedness no go overtake dem for Gibeah?
When I desire, I go chastise dem. Di peoples go dey gathered against dem, when dem dey bound to dem two transgressions.
Ephraim na heifer wey dey trained, wey love to tread out di grain. But I don pass over im fair neck. I go yoke Ephraim. Judah go plow. Jacob go break im clods.
Sow to yourselves for righteousness. Reap according to kindness. Break up your fallow ground, because na time to seek di Lord, until e come and rain righteousness on you.
Una don plow wickedness. Una don reap iniquity. Una don eat di fruit of lies, because you trust for your way, for di multitude of your mighty men.
Therefore tumult go rise among your people, and all your fortresses go dey destroyed, as Shalman destroy Beth Arbel for di day of battle. Di mother dey dashed in pieces with her children.
So Bethel go do to you because of your great wickedness. At daybreak di king of Israel go dey utterly cut off.
